name: The Chamber of Commerce
address: Southeast corner of LaSalle and Washington Streets

status.today: Office buildings stand on the corner
status.note: Burned out about 1:20 a.m. on 9 October 1871 (Andreas). What stands on the corner now is general knowledge, not researched here.

use: Board of Trade exchange and offices
summary: The Board of Trade's home, built of pale stone facing the Court House square. Grain was traded in a great hall upstairs, 44 feet high. Banks and merchants rented the floors below.

notable.text: The great triple window over the door was thirty feet high.
The flames broke in through the LaSalle Street windows and gutted it in minutes.

story.text: The corner-stone is laid before a crowd in the square.
The building is dedicated with three days of celebration.
The fire destroys it between one and two in the morning.
